newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $10 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $10 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $10 lower Monday in a technical correction to the recent sharp run-up, traders said.

New York cocoa futures rose for the fifth straight session Friday as heavy fund buying propelled the market to eight-year highs. September settled up $61 at $1,632 a tonne after setting a new life-of-contract high of $1,644. Spot July closed $69 higher at $1,592. The back months rose $67 to $69.
"The market's a little overdone," said one trader. "The market did a lot and should be poised for a correction."
Technically, September cocoa was likely to find some support in the $1,610-$1,605 range, traders said. They pegged July support at $1,565.

In London, cocoa futures were mixed at midday on Monday, easing from an early rally which drove the September contract to a fresh one-year high. LIFFE September down two stg at the break, to 1,126 stg, after peaking at 1,140 stg.
